transcript.text: Bosch built-in microwave BFL524MS0B randomly stops part way through cooking, time still on the display. Opening and closing the door lets it carry on. Maybe once every few days.

The door-interlock system is the leading suspect. A microwave that stops but retains the time, then resumes once the door has been opened and shut, commonly has an intermittent door latch/interlock switch or actuator rather than a heating fault. 1. Switch it off and unplug it. Wipe the two plastic door hooks and the matching slots in the front of the cavity with a dry cloth; check for crumbs, grease, damage or a door that appears loose or misaligned.
2. Close the door normally. It should feel firm and give a consistent positive click. If it only behaves when pushed, lifted or firmly shut, that strongly supports the interlock/latch fault. Do not remove the microwave casing or try to test the switches: internal microwave components can retain dangerous high voltage even unplugged. If the latch area looks clean and the door closes firmly, the intermittent interlock switch assembly or its wiring still needs an engineer to diagnose and repair. I would avoid using it unattended until it is checked.

I cleaned some grease from around the door hooks and latch slots, but it still happened once since. It seems to happen more when I close the door gently. The door might sit very slightly lower on the handle side, but I can't be sure. I'm not taking it out of the housing, it's screwed into the tall unit. No smell, sparks or tripping.

That can be worn latch hooks, slight door/hinge misalignment, or an internal interlock switch/actuator that is only just being operated. 1. Switch it off and unplug it. Close the door gently once normally, then once while only lightly supporting the handle side upwards — do not force or bend the door. Compare the feel and click.
2. If lifting it produces a firmer click or makes the door sit more squarely, that points to alignment/latch wear rather than a heating fault. Either way, this needs a microwave engineer rather than a DIY repair: the unit will need to be removed from the housing and the door latch, alignment and interlock-switch assembly inspected. Do not remove the casing or attempt to adjust/bypass the switches. Until repaired, avoid using it unattended; if it begins stopping more often, stop using it.

I'm not sure I could tell the difference with the lifting test, the door only looks very slightly lower and I can't be certain of that. It's out of Bosch's 2-year warranty, but I'd pay for an engineer visit if that's the next step. Is there anything else worth checking first?

There is one useful observation left, but no further worthwhile DIY dismantling check. The pattern still points most strongly to an intermittent door-interlock switch or the latch actuator that operates it; cleaning the accessible area has not cured it, and the gentle-close pattern fits a marginal latch/switch engagement. 1. Countdown freezes/pauses: this strongly supports the door-interlock/latch path, as the microwave is effectively detecting the door as open.
2. Countdown continues but heating stops: that makes an internal control or heating-circuit interruption more possible, although it still needs an engineer because the casing must not be opened. Given it is built in and you would use an engineer, booking a Bosch-approved or microwave-experienced engineer now is reasonable. Ask them to inspect the door hooks, latch actuator/alignment and interlock-switch assembly first, rather than treating it initially as a magnetron fault. Avoid leaving it running unattended until repaired.

When it stops, the time remains on the display, the 'start' indicator goes off, and the fan and light stop as if the door had been opened. I haven't watched closely enough to say whether the countdown carries on or freezes, so I can't tell you which.

Unplug it first and never remove the outer casing. That behaviour makes the door-interlock path much more likely than a heating fault: when it stops, the start indicator, fan and light all go off as though the appliance has detected that the door is open. The display retaining the time is consistent with it remaining powered but dropping out of the cooking cycle. The most likely failed item is an intermittent door interlock/monitor microswitch, or the latch actuator that operates it. A worn door hook or slight alignment issue is the other realistic cause, because it can leave the switch only marginally engaged. Cleaning the accessible latch area has not cured it, and the lifting check was inconclusive, so there is no further useful or safe DIY test. Book a Bosch-approved or microwave-experienced engineer. Tell them: “Built-in Bosch BFL524MS0B intermittently stops mid-cook; the timer stays displayed but the start symbol, fan and lamp go off, and opening then closing the door allows it to continue.” Ask them to inspect the door hooks, latch/actuator, alignment and interlock-switch assembly before investigating the high-voltage heating system. Do not remove it from the housing or open the casing yourself. Until repaired, avoid unattended use; stop using it altogether if it begins doing this frequently, fails to start reliably, or there is any burning smell, sparking or unusual noise.

candidates: Intermittent door interlock/latch switch or its actuator (high)
Intermittent control or thermal protection fault (low)
